findings.title: Interactive Keychain authorization blocks a cooperative-pool thread while holding the reader's mutation lock, ignoring the project's own readOffPool convention
findings.practice: no blocking work on the cooperative pool
findings.evidence: VendorSectionView.swift:421 `Task.detached(priority: .userInitiated) { ... try provider.authorizeCredentialsInteractively() }` -> AnthropicProvider.swift:138 -> KeychainCredentialReader.swift:88-90 `credentialMutationGate.lock(); defer {...}; let outcome = try authorize(...)`, which raises a SecurityAgent dialog and waits for the user. Task.detached still runs on the cooperative executor. AnthropicCredentialReading.swift:34-39 readOffPool() exists to avoid parking pool threads. Same pattern in OpenAIResetService (CodexResetProcess.swift:159,173; the poll loop blocks up to 15s per request).
findings.impact: While the dialog is open, a pool thread is parked with no limit. Scheduled Anthropic read() (:53-55) queues on the same NSRecursiveLock, so the Claude card stays .loading and RefreshScheduler skips ticks (Cronos RefreshScheduler:116). Separate from Cronos' planLabel() at AnthropicProvider:157.
findings.fix: Add authorizeOffPool() (continuation + DispatchQueue.global) next to readOffPool() and call it from `Task { @MainActor }`. Wrap OpenAIResetService the same way. Think about releasing the gate around the interactive prompt.

test_red_green.name: authorizeDoesNotBlockConcurrentRead
test_red_green.assert_after: authorize runs on a GCD thread; read not serialized behind the prompt

findings.cetico_evidence: VendorSectionView.swift:421 runs Task.detached (cooperative pool), which calls authorizePersistently, which holds credentialMutationGate (KeychainCredentialReader.swift:88-90) while the dialog is open. Same pattern in CodexResetProcess.swift:158/:172. Downgraded: it is triggered only by the user, who is in front of the dialog at that moment. Scheduled reads use readOffPool (a GCD thread), so they park GCD threads, not pool threads.

findings.title: ConfigLoader.onAfterSave is typed @Sendable (callable anywhere) but its only consumer traps unless it runs on MainActor
findings.evidence: ConfigLoader.swift:47,55 `struct ConfigLoader: Sendable { public var onAfterSave: @Sendable () -> Void }` invoked from nonisolated save (:111) / applyChanges (:190). AiTaskbarApp.swift:38-41 `onAfterSave = { [weak configWatcher] in MainActor.assumeIsolated { configWatcher?.adoptCurrentAsBaseline() } }`. The comment relies on 'in practice the call always lands on MainActor'.
findings.impact: The first off-main save (a background Settings save or a config migration) fails the assumeIsolated precondition and crashes. The compiler cannot catch it because the Sendable type hides the requirement.
findings.fix: Type the hook `@MainActor @Sendable () -> Void` and hop explicitly, or drop the hook and have @MainActor SettingsViewModel.save() call configWatcher.adoptCurrentAsBaseline() directly.

test_red_green.name: configSaveOffMainDoesNotTrap
test_red_green.assert_before: loader.save() from Task.detached with the production hook -> precondition crash
test_red_green.assert_after: @MainActor hook; baseline adopted after an explicit hop

findings.cetico_evidence: No off-main caller exists. save/applyChanges are called only at SettingsViewModel.swift:74 and :88, and that class is @MainActor (:11). ensureAllVendorSections writes on its own without calling onAfterSave (ConfigLoader.swift ~:276). The claimed crash needs a caller that does not exist. What remains is signature hardening (INFO).

findings.title: No project-wide checked Double->Int conversion; JWT, Anthropic credential and Gemini decoders still trap on out-of-range JSON numbers
findings.evidence: JWT.swift:52-53 `return Int(d) as? T` / `Int64(d)`; AnthropicCredentials.swift:45 `self.expiresAtMs = Int64(d)`; GeminiWireTypes.swift:154 `Int((rem * 100.0).rounded())` with rem unclamped. CostAggregator has saturatingAdd, but Sources has no Double->Int helper.
findings.impact: 1e300 is valid JSON. A float exp/expiresAt or an out-of-range agy fraction causes a SIGTRAP that decode error handling cannot catch, and it repeats on every launch while the credential/cache is unchanged. Same class as Cerbero AnthropicWireTypes:71 and the other reported sites. Fixing sites one by one keeps missing new ones.
findings.fix: Add `Int.checked(_ d: Double) -> Int?` / saturating variant in AiTaskbarCore/Util (finite + range guard or Int(exactly: d.rounded(.towardZero))). Replace every Int(/Int64( over a decoded Double with it. Add a validate.sh grep ratchet for wire types.

test_red_green.name: jwtHugeExpDoesNotTrap
test_red_green.assert_before: payload {"exp":1e300}; claim as Int crashes the process

findings.cetico_evidence: Int64(d) at AnthropicCredentials.swift:45 and Int((rem*100).rounded()) at GeminiWireTypes.swift:154 trap on 1e300. The cited JWT.swift:52-53 site is unreachable in production: the only claim calls ask for String (OpenAIProvider.swift:214, OpenAIResetProtocol.swift:47). Separate reachable site: FileCredentialReader.swift:168 Int64(timeIntervalSince1970*1000). Downgraded: every input comes from a trusted local source (a Keychain item written by the CLI, agy, a signed JWT).

findings.title: Gemini decodeSnapshot sniffs the agy payload with try?, so agy schema drift is reported as 'base_url may be wrong'
findings.evidence: :101 `if let agy = try? SharedCoders.decoder.decode(AntigravityUsageResponse.self, from: data)`. On failure it falls to GeminiModelsResponse, whose `models` is optional, and throws :129 'gemini models: response missing `models` field — base_url may be wrong'.
findings.impact: When agy renames a field, the error blames an AI Studio base_url that was never called. The real DecodingError is thrown away, which defeats the golden-test intent.
findings.fix: Branch on the payload source (tag it in fetch) or a discriminator key via JSONValue. On the agy branch, rethrow AppError.schema("agy usage decode: \(error)").

test_red_green.name: agyDriftSurfacesAgyError
test_red_green.assert_before: agy fixture with renamed groups -> message contains 'base_url may be wrong'

findings.cetico_evidence: GeminiProvider.swift:101 decodes with try?. If the agy decode fails it falls through to GeminiModelsResponse, and :127-129 throws 'base_url may be wrong'. The real DecodingError is lost.

findings.title: Relogin reset Task: the comment promises cancellation but the handle is discarded; an earlier click's timer clears a newer click's pending state
findings.practice: SwiftUI unstructured Task without lifecycle; lying comment
findings.evidence: :538-543 `let pendingReset = Task { @MainActor in try? await Task.sleep(...120s); if !Task.isCancelled { reloginPending = false } }` then `// If the view goes away, cancel the reset ... _ = pendingReset`. Nothing cancels it. Spawn issue is Fantasma's (:524).
findings.impact: Clicks at t=0 and t=100 re-enable the button at t=120, 100s early, which allows the double-spawn Fantasma described. The dead isCancelled check misleads maintainers.
findings.fix: Store it in @State and cancel the previous one plus on .onDisappear, or use .task(id: reloginAttempt) so SwiftUI owns the cancellation.
findings.cetico_evidence: The described impact (clicks at t=0 and t=100) is impossible because the button is .disabled(reloginPending) (VendorSectionView.swift:503), and reloginPending is set to true at :533 for 120 s. Only the misleading comment at :542-543 is real (INFO).

findings.title: VendorViewModel swallows UsageHistoryStore creation failure with try?, silently disabling history for the process lifetime
findings.evidence: :146 `self.historyStore = try? UsageHistoryStore.defaultFor(provider.vendorId)`. After that, recordHistory (:275 guard), the initial load and compact all no-op, with no log. (Atlas reported the binding at the same line and Cronos the :155 overwrite; this covers only the swallowed error.)
findings.impact: A dir/permission failure removes sparkline and analytics input with no log or UI signal and never retries. There is nothing to diagnose from.
findings.fix: do/catch with AppLog.lifecycle.error, plus a historyUnavailable flag. Inject the factory so tests can make it throw.

test_red_green.name: historyStoreFailureIsReported
test_red_green.assert_before: throwing factory -> indistinguishable from empty history

findings.cetico_evidence: VendorViewModel.swift:146 try? UsageHistoryStore.defaultFor(...) disables history with no log (:275 guard). The feature is best-effort, but the failure is silent, which the no-silent-try? rule forbids.

findings.title: ConfigWatcher deinit uses MainActor.assumeIsolated based on a false claim that @MainActor deinit runs on main
findings.evidence: :33-41 comment 'deinit runs on the main actor at runtime' + `MainActor.assumeIsolated { source?.cancel() }`. Nonisolated deinit runs on the releasing thread. VendorViewModel.swift:133-135 correctly says the opposite.
findings.impact: Safe only while the last reference is dropped on main (the @StateObject owner). A release off main (detached capture, background sink, test teardown) crashes in deinit, and the comment invites copying the pattern.
findings.fix: Keep the DispatchSource in a Sendable lock box and cancel it from the nonisolated deinit (cancel is thread-safe), or add an explicit stop().

test_red_green.name: configWatcherReleasedOffMainDoesNotTrap
test_red_green.assert_before: last ref released in Task.detached -> precondition failure

findings.cetico_evidence: There is a single ConfigWatcher and it lives for the whole app, owned by @StateObject (AiTaskbarApp.swift:14, :26-27). The hook captures it weakly (:38), so it is never released off main. The comment at ConfigWatcher.swift:34-36 is inaccurate, but there is no crash vector.

findings.title: NotificationService: `static var relativeFormatter` allocates on every access despite its cached-looking name; add() errors discarded
findings.evidence: :114-119 computed `private static var relativeFormatter { let f = RelativeDateTimeFormatter() ... }` vs PopoverContentView.swift:456 `static let` with the same name. :109 `UNUserNotificationCenter.current().add(req) { _ in }`. :102 English 'at' hard-coded in the title.
findings.impact: Allocates a formatter per call and misleads future hot-path callers. A failed notification is dropped silently while the threshold is still marked notified, so the user never gets it for that window.
findings.fix: Change to static let; log the error and roll back the mark on failure; localize the title.
findings.cetico_evidence: NotificationService.swift:114-119 is a computed var and :109 add(req){_ in} ignores errors. It only runs when a notification actually fires, not on a hot path, and on macOS 26 the whole path is off (:65, :94).

findings.title: Singleton wiring: MainStatusItemHolder hard-codes PinnedStatusItemManager.shared, which has a public init; itemTint(for:) ignores its argument
findings.evidence: :13-14 didSet calls `PinnedStatusItemManager.shared.mainStatusItemDidAppear()`; :134 `static let shared` with :160 `public init() {}`; :125-128 `func itemTint(for percent: Double) -> Color { return .primary }`.
findings.impact: Separately constructed managers (tests) take only the 3s-timeout path, so tests exercise different code than production. The parameter implies tinting that does not exist.
findings.fix: Inject the holder->manager signal or make init private; inline .primary.
findings.cetico_evidence: PinnedStatusItemManager.swift:13-14 hard-codes the singleton .shared. The public init (:160) is used by tests (Tests/AiTaskbarAppTests/PinnedStatusItemTests.swift:191,235), so tests go through a different path. itemTint (:125-128) ignores its parameter.

findings.title: L10n marks cache vars nonisolated(unsafe) inside a @MainActor enum, turning off checking with no need
findings.evidence: :13-14 `@MainActor public enum L10n`; :73-74 `nonisolated(unsafe) private static var cachedBundle/cachedBundleLanguage`, touched only by the main-actor `bundle` getter.
findings.impact: No race today, but a future nonisolated helper could read/write them unsynchronized without any compiler error.
findings.cetico_evidence: L10n.swift:13 marks the enum @MainActor, and :73-74 declare the caches nonisolated(unsafe). They are touched only by the @MainActor bundle getter (:76-82), so the annotation is unnecessary.
